purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Rename an asset, copy its URL, move it to a folder, or delete just this one file
finding: Right-clicking an asset in the Media drawer does not open a menu — it silently switches the whole panel into bulk-selection mode. The per-asset menu that would carry Rename, Copy URL, Copy alt text, Move to folder, Edit image, Replace across pages and Delete exists and is finished, but nothing in the drawer mounts it. So on the default Media surface there is NO way to rename a file, no way to copy its URL, and no way to move or delete a single asset without first entering a bulk mode you did not ask for.
evidence: MediaTab.tsx:16 imports MediaContextMenu and never renders it (grep of MediaTab.tsx: 1 occurrence, the import line). useMediaState.ts:342-344 returns ctxMenu/openCtxMenu/closeCtxMenu; grep across src for 'openCtxMenu', 'ctxMenu', 'MediaContextMenu' outside __tests__ returns only useMediaState + LibraryManager.tsx:495. SlimLauncher.tsx:469-476 wires onContextMenu -> props.onEnterSelection, and MediaTab.tsx:352-355 maps that to toggleSelMode+toggleSelect. Searched: 'openCtxMenu', 'ctxMenu', 'MediaContextMenu', 'onContextMenu', 'contextmenu'.
fix: Restore a per-asset menu on right-click in the drawer (the component is already built and already mounted in the fullpage manager), and give bulk selection its own visible entry — a Select control in the folder row — rather than stealing the right-click gesture for it.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Find out why a stock search returned nothing
finding: Stock search can never tell the user that it failed. The editor's stock client swallows every non-abort error and returns an empty array, and the server returns an empty array when its provider keys are unset — so 'this deployment has no Pexels/Unsplash key', 'the key expired', 'the network dropped' and 'there really are no photos of that' all render as the same silent empty grid. The failure state the code was written to show is unreachable.
evidence: StockService.ts:80-83 and :94-97 — both search methods `catch { ... return []; }`. server/services/stock.service.ts:55-56 `const key = process.env.UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY; if (!key || !query.trim()) return [];` and :102-103 the same for PEXELS_API_KEY. useDiscoveryState.ts:117-124 sets searchFailed + toasts 'Discovery search failed' only from a rejected promise, which StockService prevents. StockService.ts:54-57 admits it in a comment: 'A real configured-ness signal needs a server capability endpoint.' Searched: 'searchFailed', 'IS_STOCK_CONFIGURED', 'stockService', 'searchStockPhotos', 'PEXELS_API_KEY'.
fix: Stock needs a configured-ness signal from the server and a distinct error state in the UI: 'Stock search isn't set up on this site' is a different screen from 'No photos match beach', and only one of them is worth a retry button.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Search stock photos from the sidebar
finding: The drawer's stock browser is not wired to the failure flag at all, so even after UX-H-02 is fixed the drawer would still show a blank grid. The failure prop exists and is only passed to the other stock surface — the one that lives in the fullpage manager.
evidence: MediaTab.tsx:378-392 mounts StockBrowserOverlay with onClose/photos/videos/loading/searchQuery/orientation/color/onSearch/onSetOrientation/onSetColor/onLoadMore/onSave and no failure prop; StockBrowserOverlayProps (StockBrowserOverlay.tsx:26-38) declares none. MediaTab.tsx:243 passes searchFailed={state.searchFailed} to StockSourceModal instead. Searched: 'searchFailed', 'StockBrowserOverlay', 'onSearch'.
fix: Give the drawer's stock overlay the same three-way result state as the modal: results / genuinely empty / could not reach the provider.

screen: Media drawer · Browse stock overlay vs fullpage Library · Stock modal
purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Place a stock photo on the page
finding: There are two different stock browsers with different powers, and which one you get depends on which Media surface you happened to open. The drawer's overlay can only SAVE a photo into the library — you then have to find it in the grid and click it again to place it. The fullpage manager's modal can insert straight onto the canvas, switch provider, filter by colour, and browse icons and fonts. Nothing tells the user the other one exists.
evidence: StockBrowserOverlay.tsx:148 — the only per-cell action is `onClick={() => onSave(type, item)}`; its props (StockBrowserOverlay.tsx:26-38) carry no onInsert. MediaTab.tsx:232-249 passes onInsert={state.insertToCanvas} and onOpenIconPicker to StockSourceModal. StockBrowserOverlay.tsx:10-12 states the split in its own header comment. Searched: 'onInsert', 'onSave', 'StockSourceModal', 'StockBrowserOverlay'.
fix: One stock browser. If the drawer must be narrower, it should be the same component at a smaller size with the same actions, not a second surface missing the primary verb (place it on the page).

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Browse the full icon library, or switch stock provider
finding: A 395-line stock modal is mounted in the Media drawer behind a flag that is never turned on. Its open state is initialised false and the only call to its setter sets it to false again, so the provider switch, the colour swatches, the Icons and Fonts tabs and its 'Browse full icon library' door render for nobody in the sidebar — along with the icon-picker callback chain that hangs off it.
evidence: MediaTab.tsx:73 `const [stockModalOpen, setStockModalOpen] = React.useState(false);`; MediaTab.tsx:234 `onClose={() => setStockModalOpen(false)}` is the only other reference (grep of 'setStockModalOpen' in MediaTab.tsx returns 2 lines, both shown). MediaTab.tsx:210-224 defines handleOpenIconPicker and passes it only to that modal at :248. The drawer's Icons link instead opens IconBrowserOverlay (MediaTab.tsx:366, :393-405). Searched: 'stockModalOpen', 'setStockModalOpen', 'StockSourceModal', 'onOpenIconPicker'.
fix: Delete the unreachable mount or give it a door. Whichever survives, the Icons and Fonts entry points should sit in the same place as Upload and Browse stock — the footer — instead of being reachable only through the fullpage manager.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Upload a photo from my phone or a video from my camera
finding: The file picker offers more formats than the product can store. The upload zone accepts any image/* and any video/*, so an iPhone HEIC photo, a .avi or an .mkv are all selectable and all start uploading; the server's allow-list is a closed set of eight formats and rejects them at the token step. The user finds out their photo is the wrong format only after choosing it, from a server error, with no statement anywhere of what is actually supported.
evidence: UploadZone.tsx:15 `ACCEPT_TYPES = "image/*,video/*,.ttf,.otf,.woff,.woff2,.svg"` and :17-23 isAccepted() returns true for any file whose type starts image/ or video/. packages/dashboard/app/api/asset-upload/route.ts:31-49 ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES is png, jpeg, gif, webp, avif, svg+xml, mp4, webm, quicktime plus font types. Searched: 'ACCEPT_TYPES', 'isAccepted', 'ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES', 'image/heic', 'video/quicktime'.
fix: Make the picker's accept-list and the client-side check the same closed list the server enforces, and name the supported formats in the upload zone before the user picks — reject at choose-time with the format named, not after a round trip.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Organise a growing library into folders
finding: The drawer's folder scope button is disabled whenever the library has no folders, and the drawer has no way to create one — folder creation lives only in the fullpage manager's folder rail. So a user working in the sidebar sees a folder control that will never enable and a bulk 'Move to…' picker whose only entry is (Root), with no hint that folders exist or where to make one.
evidence: SlimLauncher.tsx:255 `disabled={(props.allFolders?.length ?? 0) === 0}` on the folder scope Button; SlimLauncher.tsx:536-548 the bulk Move-to menu renders '(Root)' plus flattenFolderTree(props.allFolders ?? []). state.createFolder is passed only at LibraryManager.tsx:354 into FolderTree, whose 'New folder' input is FolderTree.tsx:378. Searched: 'createFolder', 'onAddFolder', 'New Folder', 'allFolders'.
fix: Put New folder in the drawer's own folder menu. A disabled scope control with no reachable way to enable it is worse than no control.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Sort the library, or switch to a list view to read filenames
finding: Three controls in the drawer's folder row — Grid view, List view, Sort — are rendered permanently disabled with no tooltip and no explanation. The code says they will light up in a later task. Grid view is also drawn pressed, so the row reads as a working segmented control where two of three options simply refuse to respond. The library's sort order and sort direction are real state that nothing in the drawer can reach.
evidence: SlimLauncher.tsx:285-293 — three IconButtons, all `disabled`, the first also `pressed`; the block comment at :281-282 says 'They light up with the folder work (T12).' useMediaState.ts:363-364 exposes sort/sortDir and :372 setSort, wired nowhere in SlimLauncher. Searched: 'setSort', 'sortDir', 'List view', 'ArrowUpDown', 'disabled'.
fix: Either wire them or remove them. If they must stay, each disabled control needs a reason on hover — the repo's own Button rule says a disabled control without a stated reason is a bug.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Write alt text for an image so the published page is accessible
finding: The '✨ Generate' button for alt text fails in total silence. If the AI provider is unconfigured or the call errors, the label flips to 'Generating…', flips back to 'Generate', the field stays empty, and nothing is said. A user who presses it twice and gets nothing has no way to learn whether the feature is broken, off, or just slow.
evidence: AssetDetailOverlay.tsx:270-289 — `try { const alt = await generateContent(...) } catch { /* AI unavailable — the field stays manual. */ } finally { setAltBusy(false) }`; the catch body is a comment only. Root CLAUDE.md documents that without OPENAI_API_KEY every AI job fails on 'Missing credentials'. Searched: 'generateAlt', 'generateContent', 'altBusy', 'media-alt-generate'.
fix: Say what happened: an inline error under the field, or hide the Generate affordance entirely when AI is not configured. A magic button that does nothing teaches the user to distrust every other button on the panel.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Open a file, look at it, then rename or delete it
finding: The asset drill-in — the one screen entirely about a single file — offers no rename, no delete, no download and no copy-URL. Its five rows are Used in N places, Versions, Edit image, Optimise and Replace across site. Combined with the missing context menu (UX-H-01), a user who opens a file in the drawer, decides the name is wrong and wants it gone has to leave for the fullpage manager to do either.
evidence: AssetDetailOverlay.tsx:415-465 — the hub renders exactly five Buttons: media-detail-used, media-detail-versions, media-detail-edit, media-detail-optimize, media-detail-replace. Searched inside AssetDetailOverlay.tsx for 'Rename', 'Delete', 'Download', 'Copy URL', 'copyUrl' — no matches. useMediaState.ts:379-381 exposes renameItem and copyUrl; neither reaches this component.
fix: The detail screen is the natural home for rename, delete and download. Put them there, and let the file's name itself be the editable field.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Know which of my files will actually appear on the published site
finding: An asset that never reached the server — the upload mirror failed, or the blob token is missing — is warned about exactly twice, in two toasts that auto-dismiss: once at upload, once at insert. The grid tile itself carries no marker. A user who scrolls back an hour later cannot tell a device-only file from a real one, and placing it produces an element that renders nothing and publishes nothing.
evidence: AssetCell.tsx:64 `const badge = item.assetSource ? BADGE[item.assetSource] : undefined;` — the tile's only badge is provenance (stock/upload source), not localOnly. useUploadState.ts:121-127 and useMediaState.ts:268-277 are the two toast sites. Searched AssetCell.tsx for 'localOnly', 'offline', 'device' — no matches; grep 'localOnly' across media/ hits useMediaState.ts, useUploadState.ts, mediaTypes.ts only.
fix: Mark the tile. A device-only asset needs a persistent badge in the grid and a line in the detail screen with the action that fixes it (re-upload), not two toasts that are gone in five seconds.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: Stop an upload I started by mistake, or clear a stuck row
finding: An upload in flight in the drawer cannot be cancelled or dismissed. Each in-progress row shows a filename, a percentage and a bar, and no control at all. A 48MB video picked by accident occupies the footer until it finishes or fails; the dismiss handler exists but is only wired in the fullpage manager.
evidence: UploadZone.tsx:163-192 renders activeItems as li rows containing only the name, the percent and a progressbar — no button. Failed rows get a Retry (UploadZone.tsx:225-238) but no dismiss. state.dismissUpload is passed only at LibraryManager.tsx:379 (grep 'dismissUpload' across src outside __tests__ returns that one line plus useMediaState/useUploadState). Searched: 'dismissUpload', 'onDismissUpload', 'cancel', 'abort'.
fix: Every in-flight row needs a cancel; every terminal row needs a dismiss. Both in the drawer, where the upload was started.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: See more of my library than two columns of the sidebar
finding: The drawer's expand brackets do not widen the drawer — they close it and open a different, fullscreen screen with its own grid, folder rail, toolbar, context menu and stock modal. The user asked for more room and got a different application surface, and everything they could not do in the drawer (rename, folders, sort, single-asset delete) silently becomes possible there with no signposting that this is where those actions live.
evidence: useMediaState.ts:48-53 setPanelExpanded emits ui:media-panel-width; MediaTab.tsx:92-96 turns any panelExpanded signal into `state.setPanelExpanded(false); onOpenLibrary();`. MediaTab.tsx:87-91 block comment: 'every expand signal (the header brackets, the upload auto-expand) opens the fullpage manager instead.' MediaTab.tsx:333 wires onExpand to setPanelExpanded(true). Searched: 'panelExpanded', 'onOpenLibrary', 'setPanelExpanded', 'ui:media-panel-width'.
fix: Name the destination. If the fullpage manager is the real Media home, the drawer should say so and the actions that only exist there should be visible-but-redirecting in the drawer, rather than absent.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Unlock an element the canvas refuses to select
finding: Lock is stored in two places that never reconcile. The padlock a user sees is drawn from a per-page localStorage list; the lock the canvas enforces is a flag on the element in the project. Clicking the padlock writes both, but the panel only ever RE-READS localStorage. Open the same project in a different browser, on a different machine, or after clearing site data, and a locked element is still locked in the document — the canvas refuses to select it and tells the user to 'Unlock it in the Layers panel' — while the Layers panel draws an open padlock. The instruction points at a control that shows the opposite state.
evidence: useLayerActions.ts:70-97 hydrateFromStorage reads loadSetFromStorage(pageId,'locked') and pushes it INTO the engine (`storedLocked.forEach(id => composer.elements.getElement(id)?.setLocked(true))`) — it never reads element.isLocked() back. layersPersistence.ts:8-9 documents the keys `buildrick-layers-{pageId}-locked` / `-hidden`. useLayerActions.ts:167 `composer?.elements.getElement(pending.id)?.setLocked(pending.locked)`. Element.ts:152-153 setLocked writes this.data.locked; shared/types/element.ts:73-74 declares `locked?: boolean` on ElementData, so it travels with the document. useSelectionBehavior.ts:88-95 is the canvas refusal + that exact toast copy. Searched: 'lockedIds', 'setLocked', 'isLocked', 'loadSetFromStorage', 'buildrick-layers'.
fix: The element is the source of truth for lock. Layers should read it, not a browser-local mirror — otherwise the one control the product names as the way out of a locked element can display the wrong state.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Select a locked element
finding: Lock means two different things depending on which surface you click. Clicking a locked element on the canvas is refused with a toast. Clicking the same element's row in the Layers tree selects it normally, and the Inspector then edits it like anything else — so the lock a user set to protect an element protects it from exactly one of the two ways of reaching it.
evidence: useLayerSelection.ts:68-74 selectSingle -> `composer.selection.select(el)` with no lock check; selectLayer (:76-110) has none either. useSelectionBehavior.ts:88-95 and :106-118 both return early on `element.isLocked()` with the toast. LayerTreeItem.tsx:196-197 blocks only double-click rename on locked rows (`onDoubleClick={(e) => { if (!isLocked) onStartEditing(...) }}`); the row's onClick (:187-189) is unguarded. Searched: 'isLocked', 'lockedIds.has', 'selection.select', 'canDrag'.
fix: Decide what lock protects and apply it on both surfaces. Selecting a locked layer to inspect it is defensible — editing it silently is not; if Layers can select it, the Inspector must show it as locked with an unlock affordance.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: See at a glance which elements are hidden on mobile or tablet
finding: The Layers tree draws 'M' and 'T' badges for elements hidden at the mobile and tablet breakpoints, and they can never appear. The tree nodes are built from a five-field shape that does not include the override data the badge reads, so the field is always undefined. The result is that the Inspector's per-breakpoint Visibility switch — the one that actually removes an element from the published page at a given width — has no echo anywhere in the structural view.
evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:276-281 renders the badges from `layer.breakpointOverrides?.mobile?.hidden` / `?.tablet?.hidden`. useLayerTree.ts:88-95 buildTree returns exactly { id, type, tagName, depth, preview, children } — no breakpointOverrides. Searched: 'breakpointOverrides', 'bdc-lr-bp', 'Hidden on mobile', 'buildTree'. Confirms and extends a finding from another lane.
fix: Feed the breakpoint state into the tree node, or drop the badge. A responsive-visibility decision that is invisible in Layers is a decision the user cannot audit before publishing.

screen: Layers panel · tree row eye toggle
purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Hide an element
finding: The panel has an eye icon that does not hide anything on the site. It sets an editor-only dimming attribute on the canvas node; the element publishes exactly as before. Hiding an element from the published page is a different control in a different panel (the Inspector's Visibility section). The tooltips now say so — 'Dim in editor — the element still publishes' — but the icon is the universal symbol for hide, so the copy is fighting the glyph, and the two controls have no visible relationship to each other.
evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:285-297 the block comment and the tooltip strings 'Dim in editor — the element still publishes' / 'Show in editor — this element publishes either way'. useLayerActions.ts:126-146 toggleVisibility sets state and, in an effect, `el.setAttribute('data-hidden', ...)` on the DOM node only — nothing touches the element model or the export. Searched: 'toggleVisibility', 'data-hidden', 'hiddenIds', 'isPageLive'.
fix: One idea, one control. Either the eye drives real per-breakpoint visibility (and the Inspector reflects it), or it stops using an eye — a preview/dim affordance should not wear the icon that every other tool uses for publish-visibility.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Name my layers so the tree is readable, then hand the file to a teammate
finding: Custom layer names are browser-local. They are written to localStorage under the page id and are never part of the project, so the names a designer spends an afternoon setting are invisible to a teammate, gone on a different machine, and gone when site data is cleared. Nothing in the rename flow says this, and the write fails silently when storage is full or disabled.
evidence: useLayerActions.ts:120-124 persists customNames via saveMapToStorage(currentPageId, customNames); layersPersistence.ts:73-79 saveMapToStorage writes `buildrick-layers-{pageId}-names` inside a try/catch whose comment reads 'localStorage might be full or disabled - silently fail'. useLayerActions.ts:180-199 saveEditedName only updates the local Map and emits ELEMENT_RENAMED for the status bar. Searched: 'customNames', 'saveMapToStorage', 'ELEMENT_RENAMED', 'getDisplayName'.
fix: A layer name is document content, not a browser preference. Persist it with the element; until then the rename affordance should say the name is local to this browser.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Delete a section from the page
finding: Right-click → Delete on a layer removes the element and every descendant instantly — no confirmation, no count of what is going, and no toast afterwards. Deleting the top section of a page takes one click from a menu whose Delete row sits directly under Duplicate. The panel's multi-select banner has an inline confirm for the same act, so the safer path is the one used less often.
evidence: useLayerActions.ts:208-217 deleteLayer: beginTransaction, removeElement, endTransaction, onConfirm() — no dialog, no child count. The file's own header comment at useLayerActions.ts:8 claims 'Delete with child count confirmation'. LayerContextMenu.tsx:86-88 is the menu row. index.tsx:79 `const [pendingBannerDelete, setPendingBannerDelete]` is the banner's inline confirm, used only by LayerSelectionBanner. Searched: 'deleteLayer', 'pendingBannerDelete', 'confirm', 'removeElement'.
fix: Name the blast radius before deleting — 'Delete Section and 24 elements inside it?' — or at minimum confirm the deletion afterwards with an undo, the way Media's delete does.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Delete or duplicate several selected layers at once
finding: With five layers selected, right-clicking one of them acts on that ONE row for Cut, Copy, Duplicate, Delete and Rename, but on the whole selection for Group. The menu gives no sign which scope any item uses, and the selection stays highlighted throughout, so the user watches five highlighted rows and one of them disappear.
evidence: useLayerContextActions.ts:16-19 every case except 'group' and 'selectChildren' is keyed on the `nodeId` argument (serializeElement(nodeId), deleteLayer(nodeId,...), duplicateLayer(nodeId)); case 'group' at :97-99 uses `[...selectionHook.selectedIds]`. LayerContextMenu.tsx:20 receives selectedCount and uses it only to disable Group (:95). Searched: 'selectedIds', 'nodeId', 'LayerAction', 'groupLayers'.
fix: A context menu opened on a row inside a multi-selection should act on the selection, and should say so ('Delete 5 layers'). One menu with two silently different scopes is how people lose work.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Walk the layer tree with the keyboard
finding: Arrow keys in the tree change the canvas selection but never move keyboard focus, so the tree cannot be walked. Pressing Down once selects the row below the focused row; pressing Down again selects the same row again, because focus never left the row you started on. There is no way to step through the tree without a mouse.
evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:155-164 — ArrowDown/ArrowUp compute nextId from `visibleIds.indexOf(layer.id)` (the row that owns the handler) and call `onSelect(nextId, {})`; there is no focus() call. grep for '.focus()' across panels/layers/index.tsx, LayerTreeItem.tsx and hooks/ returns exactly one hit, useLayerActions.ts:175, which focuses the rename input. index.tsx:180-186 scrollToSelection only scrolls. Searched: 'ArrowDown', 'focus()', 'getVisibleLayerIds', 'roving', 'tabIndex'.
fix: Move focus with the arrow keys and let selection follow focus (or follow on Enter). This is the standard tree pattern and the panel already declares role=tree/treeitem.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Tab past the Layers panel to reach the canvas or the Inspector
finding: Every layer row is its own tab stop, and each row also contains up to three more focusable buttons (chevron, eye, lock). On a page with 80 elements that is over 200 presses of Tab to get out of the panel. A keyboard user cannot leave Layers in any reasonable number of keystrokes.
evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:172 `tabIndex={0}` on the treeitem div — unconditional, one per row. The chevron Button (:200-206) sets tabIndex={-1} only when the row has no children; the eye (:301-311) and lock (:324-333) Buttons set no tabIndex at all and are native buttons. index.tsx:428 declares role='tree' on the container. Searched: 'tabIndex', 'role="treeitem"', 'roving', 'aria-activedescendant'.
fix: One tab stop for the whole tree (roving tabindex or aria-activedescendant), with the row actions reachable from the focused row rather than each being its own stop.

screen: Layers panel · tree row eye/lock buttons
purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Hide or lock the layer I am pointing at
finding: The old defect where 40px controls sat in 28px rows — so a click on the eye landed on the wrong layer — is FIXED: the buttons are now 20x20 inside a 28px row. What remains is that 20x20 is under the 24x24 minimum for a pointer target, and the row has the height to give it: two controls that toggle state on the wrong element are still a mis-click that a user may not notice.
evidence: styles/layers-v2.css:157-168 — the comment reads 'Before: 40px controls in 28px rows, and elementFromPoint at…' and the rule now sets width/height 20px, min-height 0, padding 2px on .bdc-lr .bdc-lr-eye and .bdc-lr-lock. styles/layers-v2.css:17-27 .bdc-lr height 28px, padding 0 8px. LayerTreeItem.tsx:110-118 indent ladder base 12 step 16, matching the brief. Searched: 'bdc-lr-eye', 'bdc-lr-lock', 'elementFromPoint', 'height: 20px'.
fix: Take the row's full 24px of usable height for both toggles. The regression is fixed; the target is still smaller than the guidance for a control whose mis-click silently changes a different element.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Move an element into a different container by dragging its layer row
finding: A refused drop explains itself in raw type names and then vanishes. 'text cannot be nested inside heading' and 'button cannot contain children' are the element type ids, not the names the user sees on the rows, and the message clears itself after three seconds whether or not it was read. A locked container refuses a drop with a message but the row shows no locked-target affordance during the drag.
evidence: index.tsx:120-135 showDropError('Cannot drop inside a locked container'), `${parentType} cannot contain children`, `${sourceType} cannot be nested inside ${parentType}` — parentType/sourceType come straight from getType(). index.tsx:87-93 auto-clears dropFeedback after 3000ms. LayerTreeItem.tsx:180-186 sets no drop-refused styling on the target row; data-drop only carries before/after/inside. Searched: 'showDropError', 'dropFeedback', 'canNestElement', 'data-drop'.
fix: Say it in the words on the row ('A Heading can't hold other elements'), show the refusal on the target row during the drag rather than after the drop, and let the message stay until the user moves on.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: Find every layer that is currently hidden or locked, or clear all locks
finding: Hide and lock are per-row toggles with no roll-up anywhere. The footer counts total and selected layers only, so a user who locked six things across a long page has no way to find them again except by scrolling the whole tree, and no way to clear them in one move. Search matches names and types, not state.
evidence: LayersTab.tsx:216-221 the footer renders only `${stats.selected} selected of ${stats.total}` or `${stats.total} layers`; stats come from index.tsx:63-67 which emits { total, selected } and nothing else. LayersTab.tsx:176-184 the header's three buttons are Expand all, Collapse all, Display settings. useLayerSearch.ts itemMatches is name/type based. Searched: 'stats-change', 'hiddenIds.size', 'lockedIds.size', 'Expand all', 'itemMatches'.

screen: Brand › Import / export · IMPORT · Resolve conflicts
purpose: Brand is the site-builder design system — the colour, type, spacing and component tokens that style the CUSTOMER's published site, not the editor's own chrome.
task: Import a token file into a brand I have already customised
finding: The conflict box says 'Choose how to handle them' when a choice has already been made for the user, and it is the overwriting one. Replace is pre-selected the moment a file parses and again on every reset, so a user who reads '12 tokens already exist with the same ID', presses the primary button and never touches the two chips has silently overwritten twelve of their own brand values. The button they press reads 'Apply 12 valid only' — the word 'only' reads as the cautious option while the active strategy is the destructive one.
evidence: ImportCard.tsx:126 `React.useState<ConflictStrategy>("replace")`; ImportCard.tsx:188 `setStrategy("replace")` at the end of ingestRaw; ImportCard.tsx:208 the same on Cancel. ImportCard.tsx:213-221 handleApply sends every token unless strategy === 'keep-mine'. ImportCard.tsx:365-393 the resolve box and its two chips. ImportCard.tsx:400-403 the Apply button label. Searched: 'ConflictStrategy', 'setStrategy', 'keep-mine', 'handleApply', 'conflictCount'.
fix: Default to the non-destructive strategy, or default to nothing and disable Apply until the user chooses. A screen that asks a question and pre-answers it with the irreversible option is not asking.

screen: Brand › Import / export · IMPORT · detail block
purpose: Brand is the site-builder design system — the colour, type, spacing and component tokens that style the CUSTOMER's published site, not the editor's own chrome.
task: Decide whether to accept an incoming token file
finding: The conflict is reported as a bare number — '12 ID collisions' — and never as a list. There is no way to see WHICH of your tokens are about to be overwritten, what their current values are, what the incoming values are, or to accept some and refuse others. The decision the screen asks for cannot be made from what the screen shows.
evidence: ImportCard.tsx:356-362 renders `${conflictCount} ID collisions` and nothing else; conflictCount is `parsed.diff.modified.length` (:239). diffTokens already computes the full modified list (imported at :26 from importUtils, used at :180) — the per-token data exists and is never displayed. The strategy is a single global choice (ImportCard.tsx:41 `type ConflictStrategy = "replace" | "keep-mine"`). Searched: 'diff.modified', 'diffTokens', 'DiffResult', 'conflictCount'.
fix: Show the collisions as rows — token name, your value, their value — with a per-row keep/take. The whole-file strategy chips can stay as bulk shortcuts over that list.

screen: Brand › Import / export · IMPORT · drop zone

screen: Brand › Import / export · IMPORT · detail block
purpose: Brand is the site-builder design system — the colour, type, spacing and component tokens that style the CUSTOMER's published site, not the editor's own chrome.
task: See whether part of my token file was rejected
finding: The 'Errors' row in the import summary can only ever read 0. Any parse error clears the parsed state entirely and routes to a separate error box, so by the time the summary renders, its error list is guaranteed empty. A file where some tokens are valid and some are malformed reports as clean.
evidence: ImportCard.tsx:172-186 ingestRaw — on `parsedJson.errors.length > 0` it sets parseErrors, calls setParsed(null) and returns; otherwise it builds the ParsedState with a literal `errors: []` (:183). ImportCard.tsx:346-354 renders the Errors row from `parsed.errors`, which is therefore always []. Searched: 'parsed.errors', 'parseErrors', 'ingestRaw', 'ParsedState'.
fix: Carry per-token rejections into the summary and name them, so 'Valid tokens 40' can sit next to a truthful 'Errors 3 — heading-xl, radius-pill, shadow-soft'.

purpose: Media is where a site's images, video, icons and fonts are uploaded, organised, described and placed on the canvas.
task: All media tasks
finding: PURPOSE: hold every non-text asset a site uses and get it onto the page. PRIMARY TASKS: upload files; find an asset (search, type pills, folders, load-more paging); place it on the canvas by click or drag; describe it (alt text); replace one asset with another across the whole site; optimise or edit an image; delete safely. ENTRY POINTS: the rail's Media tab (MediaTab -> SlimLauncher at 320); the header expand brackets, which do not widen the drawer but open the fullpage LibraryManager instead (MediaTab.tsx:92-96); and two engine events that push the user in from elsewhere — `ui:media-selection-request` and `element:needs-asset`, both of which emit `ui:switch-tab` to 'assets' and pre-filter the panel (useMediaState.ts:117-155). EXIT POINTS: inserting emits `ui:switch-tab` back to 'add' in selection mode (useMediaState.ts:240); the drill-in's Used-in view jumps to a page and element on the canvas; Close on the panel header. HANDS OFF TO: canvas (insertMediaAt / replaceMedia via composer.mediaOps), inspector (a placed image's own properties), pages (the used-in jump), publish (localOnly assets never reach it). RECEIVES FROM: canvas/build (the empty-media-element contract that opens the picker), inspector (media-selection-request), the dashboard's asset-upload route and the stock proxy. THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: the module has two surfaces with unequal powers — a 320 drawer that is the default and a fullpage manager that holds rename, folders, sort, single-asset delete, the richer stock browser and the context menu — and nothing in the drawer names the second one or explains why an action is missing.
evidence: MediaTab.tsx:83-96 and :299-306 (the fullpage branch is unreachable from this component); useMediaState.ts:117-155 (the two inbound events); LibraryManager.tsx:354-379, :467-468, :495 (the actions only it wires). Searched: 'ui:switch-tab', 'ui:media-selection-request', 'element:needs-asset', 'onOpenLibrary', 'MEDIA_EVENTS'.
fix: Make one Media surface canonical and let the other be a size of it. Every action the drawer cannot perform should either be present there or visibly point at where it lives.

purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
task: All layers tasks
finding: PURPOSE: show the current page as a tree so a user can find, name, reorder and protect elements that are hard to hit on the canvas. PRIMARY TASKS: locate an element (search, expand/collapse all, auto-expand to the selection); select one or several; rename; reorder by drag; hide (editor-only dimming) and lock; cut/copy/paste/duplicate/delete/group from the right-click menu; copy a deep link to an element. ENTRY POINTS: the rail's Layers tab (LayersTab -> LayersPanel); a canvas selection auto-expands ancestors and scrolls the row into view (index.tsx:189-200); `layers:expand-all` / `layers:collapse-all` from the tab header. EXIT POINTS: selecting a row drives the canvas and the Inspector; the empty state's 'Open Insert' link hands off to Insert (LayersEmptyState.tsx:26-33); Copy link produces a URL that reopens the editor on this element. HANDS OFF TO: canvas + inspector (selection is the shared object, composer.selection is SSOT), engine history (every structural action wraps beginTransaction/endTransaction). RECEIVES FROM: canvas (selection, hover highlight), pages (a page change rebuilds the tree and re-reads that page's stored state), components (the instance badge). THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: three of the panel's own concepts — lock, hide and custom names — live in per-page localStorage rather than in the document, so the tree can disagree with the engine, with the canvas and with a teammate; and the panel is not keyboard-operable in the way its own role=tree markup promises.
evidence: index.tsx:47-77, :189-200; LayersTab.tsx:113-126 (stats), :138-142 (expand/collapse events); layersPersistence.ts:8-9 (the three localStorage keys); useLayerTree.ts:99-105 (page-change rebuild); useLayerSelection.ts:43-66 (composer selection mirror). Searched: 'layers:stats-change', 'layers:expand-all', 'buildrick-layers', 'role="tree"', 'SELECTION_ADDED'.
fix: Move lock, hide and layer names into the document so the tree, the canvas and a teammate cannot disagree, and give the tree the roving-focus keyboard behaviour its role=tree markup already promises.

purpose: Brand is the site-builder design system — the colour, type, spacing and component tokens that style the CUSTOMER's published site, not the editor's own chrome.
task: All brand tasks
finding: PURPOSE: own the design system of the customer's published site — fourteen token kinds plus component style presets — as one place, so a site's look changes from one screen rather than element by element. NOTE THE BOUNDARY: this is `--buildrick-design-*`, the customer's tokens; the editor's own `--bk-*` chrome tokens are generated from Figma and are a different system entirely. PRIMARY TASKS: pick a starting point (6 starters); edit tokens by kind; manage component presets and shared classes; set light/dark values; read lint; import and export a token file. ENTRY POINTS: the rail's Design/Brand tab, which opens a drill-in root of nine destinations (DesignSystemTab.tsx:134-149); `ProjectTokensApplier` puts the site's tokens on the page at project load, independent of the panel. EXIT POINTS: the footer's Save (DesignTabFooter.tsx:20 APPLY_CHANGES_LABEL) commits through a Review modal to setProjectSettings + persistAll; Discard reverts every registry. HANDS OFF TO: canvas (every edit writes its CSS var to document.documentElement immediately, so the canvas IS the live preview — useTokenBase.ts:64), publish (projectSettings.designTokens), inspector (tokens offered as values). RECEIVES FROM: the engine's settings events and the token-usage tracker (which elements consume which token). THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: the staging model is sound — edits preview live and commit behind one Save — but the three doors that write the WHOLE brand at once (starters, import, and the AI generate button that ships past its own feature flag) all commit without showing the user what they are about to replace.
evidence: DesignSystemTab.tsx:134-149 (the nine destinations), :562-578 (handleDiscard), :495-505 (the guard that was removed and why); useTokenBase.ts:64,124,145 (live CSS-var writes + discard restore); ProjectTokensApplier.tsx:29-60; DesignTabFooter.tsx:20-21. The FEATURE_DS_AI gap (useComposerInit.ts:132 gates the client, DesignSystemTab.tsx:890 does not gate the button) is carried from another lane and was not re-derived here. Searched: 'DesignSection', 'SECTIONS', 'discardAll', 'setProjectSettings', 'designTokens'.
